metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: Permissions-Policy header missing finding template with comprehensive guidance for all audiences including framework-specific implementation code, server configurations, and testing strategies to control which browser features and APIs can be used by the application and embedded third-party content, preventing unauthorized access to sensitive device capabilities like camera, microphone, geolocation, and payment APIs.

EXECUTIVE.summary: Your application lacks Permissions-Policy protection, allowing unrestricted access to powerful browser features like camera, microphone, location tracking, and payment APIs, which third-party scripts and embedded content could exploit without explicit authorization.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: Medium risk of privacy violations and unauthorized feature access. Without Permissions-Policy, embedded third-party content (ads, analytics, widgets) can potentially: access device camera/microphone without user awareness, track precise geolocation, initiate payment requests, access USB devices, enable fullscreen mode unexpectedly, autoplay media consuming bandwidth. Privacy-focused industries (healthcare, finance, education) face elevated compliance risk. Malicious or compromised third-party scripts could abuse powerful APIs. GDPR Article 25 requires privacy by design. Risk increases with: multiple third-party integrations, advertising networks, social media widgets, analytics platforms. Potential for user trust erosion and regulatory scrutiny.
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: GDPR Article 25 (Data Protection by Design and Default) recommends minimizing feature access. Browser security best practices from W3C. Privacy regulations may require demonstrating control over third-party capabilities. Growing regulatory focus on third-party risk management. Security frameworks increasingly expect Permissions-Policy as baseline control.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: Missing Permissions-Policy header allows third-party scripts and embedded content unrestricted access to powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payments). Need to implement restrictive policy to control feature access.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: Should be addressed within current or next sprint. Implementation takes 1-2 hours including testing and policy configuration. Medium complexity - requires understanding which features application uses. Medium priority, higher for privacy-sensitive industries or applications with significant third-party integrations.
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 1-2 hours for initial implementation. Additional 1-2 hours for testing and refinement based on legitimate feature requirements. Ongoing maintenance as features added.
dependencies: Inventory of application features used (camera, geolocation, etc.)
List of third-party integrations and their feature requirements
Access to web server or application configuration

DEVELOPER.summary: Permissions-Policy HTTP response header is not present, allowing all browser features and powerful APIs to be used by any origin without restriction, including embedded third-party content.
DEVELOPER.technical: Permissions-Policy (formerly Feature-Policy) is an HTTP response header that allows/denies use of browser features and APIs in the application and embedded iframes. Without this header, all features are allowed by default. Controls powerful capabilities: geolocation, camera, microphone, payment, usb, midi, accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, fullscreen, autoplay, picture-in-picture, display-capture, document-domain, encrypted-media, execution-while-not-rendered, execution-while-out-of-viewport, and more. Syntax: Permissions-Policy: feature=(allowlist). Directives: 'self' (same origin), 'none' (deny all), * (allow all), specific origins (https://example.com). Replaces deprecated Feature-Policy header. Supported by modern browsers (Chrome 88+, Edge 88+, Opera 74+). Firefox has partial support. Safari limited support.
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: CWE-276 (Incorrect Default Permissions), CWE-862 (Missing Authorization). Without Permissions-Policy, embedded third-party content inherits all feature permissions. Attack scenarios: (1) Malicious ad network script accesses camera/microphone, (2) Compromised analytics code tracks precise geolocation, (3) Widget initiates unauthorized payment requests, (4) Embedded iframe accesses USB devices, (5) Third-party script enables fullscreen for phishing overlay. Risk elevated when: multiple third-party scripts, advertising networks, social media embeds, untrusted CDN content, iframe-based integrations. Defense-in-depth control preventing feature abuse even if XSS or third-party compromise occurs.

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: Missing Permissions-Policy enables unauthorized browser feature and API access by third-party content, creating privacy violations and potential exploitation of powerful device capabilities without explicit permission control.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: CWE-276 (Incorrect Default Permissions), CWE-862 (Missing Authorization for Critical Function). Permissions-Policy provides defense-in-depth against: malicious third-party scripts, compromised CDN content, advertising network abuse, social media widget overreach, iframe-based attacks. Without policy, all powerful browser APIs available to any embedded content. Exploitable features: camera (surveillance), microphone (eavesdropping), geolocation (precise tracking), payment (unauthorized transactions), usb (device access), fullscreen (phishing overlays), autoplay (resource consumption), picture-in-picture (persistent tracking). Attack vectors amplified by: XSS vulnerabilities enabling feature abuse, compromised third-party dependencies, malvertising campaigns, supply chain attacks on analytics/ad platforms.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: Passive or active exploitation through third-party content. Passive: Compromised or malicious third-party script (analytics, ads, widgets) uses allowed features without user awareness. Active: XSS vulnerability allows attacker to inject script that accesses powerful APIs. Scenarios: (1) Malicious ad accesses camera, records user without consent, (2) Compromised analytics tracks precise geolocation continuously, (3) Widget initiates payment request mimicking legitimate transaction, (4) Fullscreen API used for convincing phishing overlay, (5) Autoplay abuse drains mobile data. No direct application vulnerability needed - third-party risk is sufficient attack surface. User interaction may trigger but features accessible without explicit permission dialog in some contexts.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: MEDIUM - Severity depends on third-party integration extent and feature sensitivity. Critical if: camera/microphone access allowed, payment APIs enabled, extensive third-party scripts, advertising networks integrated, user-generated content with embeds. Growing importance as browsers implement more powerful APIs. Recommended for all applications as defense-in-depth, mandatory for privacy-sensitive industries. Simple implementation with minimal functional risk if policy properly configured. Start restrictive, relax as needed based on legitimate requirements.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: Implement within 2-4 weeks as part of security header hardening. Higher priority (1-2 weeks) if: multiple third-party integrations, advertising networks, privacy-sensitive industry (healthcare, finance, education), camera/microphone features used, payment processing, GDPR compliance required. Low implementation complexity but requires feature inventory. Begin with restrictive policy, monitor for breakage, adjust as needed.

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: Web servers not configured to send Permissions-Policy header, requiring HTTP response header configuration to control browser feature access and restrict third-party capability usage.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: Permissions-Policy header must be added to HTTP responses at web server, reverse proxy, or application layer. Header syntax: Permissions-Policy: feature1=(allowlist1), feature2=(allowlist2). Common restrictive policy: Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=(). Allow specific features for same-origin: Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(self), camera=(self). Typically configured in Nginx, Apache, load balancers, CDN, or application middleware. Consider impact on: third-party analytics (may use features), advertising (interest-cohort for FLoC), social media widgets, payment integrations, video conferencing features.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: All web servers serving application traffic: production web servers, load balancers, CDN origin shields, API gateways, reverse proxies. Must be consistent across all environments (dev, staging, production). Applies to all HTTP responses. Consider different policies for: pages with video conferencing (allow camera/microphone), payment pages (allow payment API), public pages (most restrictive), embedded content (iframe sandbox).
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: Monitor for feature access errors after implementation. Use browser DevTools console to identify blocked features. Check error logs for Permissions-Policy violations. Test critical features still function (maps, payment, video calls). Monitor third-party integrations for breakage. Include in regular security header audits. Browser support varies - test across browsers.

QA_TESTER.summary: Missing Permissions-Policy header prevents validation that browser feature access is properly controlled and third-party content cannot abuse powerful APIs without authorization.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Cannot validate feature access controls. Security testing tools flag missing Permissions-Policy as medium-severity finding. After implementation, must test: (1) Header present on all responses, (2) Application features requiring permissions still work (camera, location, etc.), (3) Third-party integrations function correctly, (4) Payment processing works if applicable, (5) Video conferencing features functional, (6) Maps and geolocation services work, (7) No broken functionality from restricted features.
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Security audit finding (medium severity). Privacy compliance gap. Unauthorized feature access vulnerability. Third-party scripts can abuse powerful APIs. Potential GDPR Article 25 violation. User privacy not adequately protected. No control over embedded content capabilities. Increased attack surface through third-party integrations.

generic.code:
# Generic Permissions-Policy Implementation Guidelines

## Header Syntax

Permissions-Policy: feature1=(allowlist1), feature2=(allowlist2), ...

## Allowlist Values

() or 'none'          - Deny for all origins (most restrictive)
(self) or 'self'      - Allow for same origin only
*                     - Allow for all origins (least restrictive)
https://example.com   - Allow for specific origin

## Common Features to Control

### High-Risk Features (Restrict by default)
- geolocation     - GPS location access
- camera          - Camera access
- microphone      - Microphone access
- payment         - Payment Request API
- usb             - USB device access
- serial          - Serial port access
- hid             - HID device access

### Privacy Features
- interest-cohort - Google FLoC tracking (set to 'none')

### Media Features
- autoplay        - Autoplay media
- fullscreen      - Fullscreen API
- picture-in-picture - PiP mode
- display-capture - Screen sharing

### Sensor Features
- accelerometer   - Motion sensor
- gyroscope       - Orientation sensor
- magnetometer    - Compass
- ambient-light-sensor - Light sensor

## Example Policies

### 1. Maximum Security (Deny Everything)
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=(), \
  payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()

### 2. Standard Web Application
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(self), camera=(), microphone=(), \
  payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=(), fullscreen=(self)

### 3. Video Conferencing Application
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(self), camera=(self), \
  microphone=(self), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=(), \
  fullscreen=(self), display-capture=(self)

### 4. E-commerce with Payment API
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(self), camera=(), microphone=(), \
  payment=(self), usb=(), interest-cohort=(), fullscreen=(self)

### 5. Map/Location Application
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(self), camera=(), microphone=(), \
  payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()

### 6. Disable FLoC Only (Minimum)
Permissions-Policy: interest-cohort=()

## Feature Selection Guide

### Start with restrictive policy:
1. Deny all features: geolocation=(), camera=(), etc.
2. Deploy to staging
3. Test all application features
4. Identify which features actually needed
5. Relax policy for required features only
6. Deploy to production
7. Monitor for errors

### Common feature requirements:
- Maps/Navigation → geolocation=(self)
- Video calls → camera=(self), microphone=(self)
- Payments → payment=(self)
- Media sites → fullscreen=(self), picture-in-picture=(self)
- Screen sharing → display-capture=(self)

## Implementation Checklist

✅ Inventory features your application uses
✅ Start with restrictive policy (deny all)
✅ Test all features in staging
✅ Allow only required features
✅ Always disable interest-cohort (FLoC)
✅ Test third-party integrations
✅ Document policy decisions
✅ Review policy when adding features

# Generic Permissions-Policy Testing

## Browser DevTools Testing

1. Open browser DevTools (F12)
2. Go to Network tab
3. Navigate to your site
4. Click on main document request
5. Go to Headers section
6. Look for Permissions-Policy in Response Headers
7. Verify policy includes key features

## Feature Access Testing

### Test Geolocation Block
1. Open browser console
2. Try to access geolocation:
   navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(
     pos => console.log('Allowed:', pos),
     err => console.log('Blocked:', err)
   );
3. Should see permission denied if blocked

### Test Camera Block
1. Open browser console
2. Try to access camera:
   navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ video: true })
     .then(() => console.log('Camera allowed'))
     .catch(() => console.log('Camera blocked'));
3. Should fail if camera=() in policy

### Test Payment API Block
1. Open browser console
2. Check if Payment Request API available:
   console.log('PaymentRequest' in window);
3. Try to create payment request (will fail if blocked)

## Command-Line Testing

# Check if Permissions-Policy header present
curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i permissions-policy

# Expected output:
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=(), ...

## Online Testing Tools

1. Security Headers Scanner
   https://securityheaders.com/
   - Enter domain
   - Verify Permissions-Policy present

2. Mozilla Observatory
   https://observatory.mozilla.org/
   - Comprehensive security scan

## Automated Testing Script

#!/bin/bash
# test-permissions-policy.sh

URL="$1"

if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <url>"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Testing Permissions-Policy for: $URL"

PP=$(curl -s -I "$URL" | grep -i "^permissions-policy:" | cut -d: -f2-)

if [ -z "$PP" ]; then
  echo "❌ Permissions-Policy header is MISSING"
  exit 1
else
  echo "✅ Permissions-Policy present"
  echo "Policy: $PP"
  
  # Check for sensitive features
  for feature in geolocation camera microphone payment usb; do
    if echo "$PP" | grep -q "$feature"; then
      echo "✅ $feature policy set"
    else
      echo "âš ï¸ $feature not in policy"
    fi
  done
  
  # Check FLoC disabled
  if echo "$PP" | grep -q "interest-cohort=()"; then
    echo "✅ FLoC disabled (interest-cohort)"
  else
    echo "âš ï¸ Consider disabling FLoC"
  fi
fi

apache.config:
# Apache - Add Permissions-Policy header
# /etc/apache2/sites-available/your-site.conf or .htaccess

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName your-domain.com
    
    # Enable mod_headers
    # a2enmod headers
    
    # Restrictive Permissions-Policy
    Header always set Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()"
    
    # Alternative: Allow specific features
    # Header always set Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(self), camera=(self), microphone=(self), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()"
    
    # Other security headers
    Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
    Header always set X-Frame-Options "DENY"
    
    DocumentRoot /var/www/html
    
    # Optional: Directory-specific policies
    <Directory /var/www/html/video-call>
        Header always set Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(self), camera=(self), microphone=(self), payment=()"
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>

# .htaccess alternative
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  Header always set Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()"
</IfModule>
apache.reload:
# Enable headers module
sudo a2enmod headers

# Test configuration
sudo apachectl configtest

# Reload Apache
sudo systemctl reload apache2

# Verify running
sudo systemctl status apache2
apache.verify:
# Verify header present
curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i permissions-policy

# Verify headers module loaded
apachectl -M | grep headers

aws-cloudfront.reload:
# No reload needed - CloudFront propagates automatically

# Check deployment (5-15 minutes)
aws cloudfront wait distribution-deployed --id DISTRIBUTION_ID
aws-cloudfront.verify:
# Test header from CloudFront
curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i permissions-policy

# Expected output:
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), ...

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
1. Keep backup of configuration files
2. Document current header configuration
3. If Permissions-Policy breaks features (video calls, maps, payments), temporarily adjust policy
4. For Nginx: Edit header line, test with 'nginx -t', reload
5. For Apache: Edit header line, test with 'apachectl configtest', reload
6. For AWS CloudFront: Update Response Headers Policy value
7. Identify which feature broke (geolocation, camera, microphone, payment)
8. Allow specific feature: change () to (self) for that feature
9. Re-deploy with adjusted policy
10. Test affected functionality thoroughly

11. Monitor browser console for Permissions-Policy errors
12. Verify no broken functionality for 24-48 hours
